dna.note: intrusion is a NEW word. `facture` (capsule, dome, folded_strip, platonic_grabbables, triangleprofiles - cast|facet|armature|section|wear) is the nearest relative and was refused: facture asks how a thing was fabricated, which presumes a maker, and this asks how much of a mathematical object survives being written into a noise pipeline. `weather`, `provenance`, `authorship`, `derivation` and `descent` are each already held with another meaning. The rungs are the three strengths as a LADDER rather than three knobs, and they were sized on a numpy replica of evaluate() over the same 65^3 corner grid at the scene's own iso_level of 1.0, counting connected bodies: melted (4.0, 0.5, 1.0) SHIPPED shatters the lattice into 2,859 separate bodies with no period readable anywhere in the box; formula (0, 0, 0) is ONE connected body holding 100% of the solid, every unit cell identical; eroded (0, 0.5, 0) keeps the period and pits the sheets - 1,268 bodies, but 95.3% of the solid still in one piece, a lattice surviving its own wear; drifting (0, 0.5, 1.0) restores only the space-varying threshold, so sheets thicken in some regions and thin to holes in others. 1 body against 2,859 is the axis in one number. SAID PRECISELY, because the registry's own description does not and the difference is the sequence's subject: `formula` is the pure gyroid level set at THIS ARTIFACT'S threshold, g = iso_level = 1.0, not the balanced minimal surface g = 0. GyroidDemo.tscn sets iso_level 1.0 and that export is untouched here, so what formula shows is the mathematical object at the threshold somebody already chose - which is the more honest picture for a sequence whose truth line is that the boundary between inside and outside is a decision. period is also NEW. `grain` (grabbable_line and 5 others - solid|split|quartered|lattice|shell) asks how the mass inside a fixed silhouette is divided, which is close, but its five rungs cannot be built here; `unit` (diamonds), `cell` (tessellation_lattice_demo) and `pitch_space` (harmonic_distance_table) are taken with other meanings. baseScale 0.5 against chunk_scale 20 gives ~1.59 periods per axis, and the multiplier is applied ONLY to the gyroid term's coordinate - deliberately NOT to baseScale, which also feeds the warp and the erosion, so scaling it would confound the two axes. Written this way the pair is strictly orthogonal: intrusion varies what is ADDED to the field with the period held, period varies the period with the additions held. pair 1.0 SHIPPED (~1.6 periods, two half-cells reading as a pair of sheets); sheet 0.5 (~0.8 periods, less than one full cell - the picture that shows the gyroid is a SURFACE and not a lattice); lattice 2.0 (~3.2 periods, the repeat unmistakable); weave 4.0 (~6.4 periods, a fine three-way interpenetrating weave). Both axes reach the GPU by the pattern TerrainGeneratorShapes already uses for shapeId: get_params_array() calls super and appends four floats, ParamsBuffer gains four matching trailing fields. MarchingGyroid.glsl is loaded by TerrainGeneratorGyroid and by nothing else, and TerrainGeneratorGyroid is loaded by GyroidDemo.tscn and by nothing else, so the shared eleven-field prefix every other Marching*.glsl reads is untouched by construction.

dna.note: Every other field in this sequence is GIVEN: gyroid_demo's by a formula, animated_noise_explorer's by noise, fifteen_cases_demo's by a lookup table, metaballs' by a fixed set of sources. This one's is DEPOSITED - a hand puts material in and the extractor finds a boundary through whatever was put - so its axis is what the hand did, and no other artifact here can carry that claim. All four rungs use THE SAME SEVEN DEPOSITS: the same six radii from the generator's own fractions (0.5/0.35/0.25/0.22/0.18/0.15 of s = chunk_scale * 0.15) plus the same centre deposit at the literal 0.3. The amount of material, the threshold and the sampling do not move between rungs; only the arrangement does, which is what makes this an axis about arrangement and nothing else. stack is the shipped standing form. sweep drags the seven along one horizontal arc that rises and settles, heavy end at +x/-z tapering to -x/+z. dab pushes them to seven of the volume's eight corners, spaced so that no two extracted surfaces touch - seven separate closed surfaces where every other rung gives one, which is the honest picture of what a deposit IS before anything fuses it, and the rung that carries the claim: the extractor did not build a body, it found the boundary of what was there. heap piles them low around the floor with the top half of the box empty. WHY THE dab NUMBERS ARE NOT FREE. iso_level is 0.3 against a plain sphere SDF, so every deposit renders at radius r + 0.3 - the smallest of the seven is a 0.345 ball and the largest a 0.6 ball, inside a box of half-extent 1.0 - and opSmoothUnion at k = scale * 0.06 = 0.12 bridges any two surfaces whose gap is under k/2 = 0.06. Each dab position is pushed to 0.96 - (r + 0.3) per axis, as close to the wall as the deposit can sit without the sampled domain clipping it, and the two SMALLEST deposits take the corners adjacent to the big one because that pair sets the tightest gap. The result, computed rather than hoped: minimum surface gap 0.073 and every other pair at 0.21 or more, so dab separates with about 20% margin on the worst pair. These numbers are tuned against the shipped volume_size 2.0 and iso_level 0.3; they scale with chunk_scale and they do NOT survive a change of iso_level. THE WORD. `hand` is taken from sculpt_one (randomness.json: composition|pour|drape|stipple|spatter, which procedure makes the form) and from maze_generation (procgen_extra.json: which algorithm builds the maze). The corpus already treats it as a stable word with artifact-specific rungs, the same licence `trace` carries across spring_demo and fourier_transform. sculpt_one's own five rungs are not answerable here - this tool deposits only spheres - so the rungs are this artifact's own moves, which is what that precedent requires.

dna.finding: NO SEED EXPORT WAS ADDED AND NONE SHOULD BE. The audit's 14 random calls are real and every one of them is in an interactive path - _input's KEY_R branch and the mouse-button handler, and _regenerate_sculpture's three randf_range pairs behind the REGEN button. None of them runs during a capture, the build path contains no randf at all, and the four rungs are literal position tables. Adding a seed would imply a randomness this axis does not use. If anyone later makes dab or heap SCATTER, law 4 applies immediately and a seed export plus a dna.fixture pin becomes mandatory. THE REAL DETERMINISM HAZARD IS THE COMPUTE PATH AND IT IS SILENT, exactly as on mc_shapes_gallery: TerrainGeneratorBase._ready falls back when RenderingServer.create_local_rendering_device() or the SPIR-V load fails, and TerrainGeneratorSculpt inherits an EMPTY _create_fallback_mesh(), so a host without a working local rendering device publishes four blank frames and the critic files a live axis as INERT or NO RENDER. Before believing any verdict on this token, grep the sweep's stdout for 'Compute initialization failed'. The synchronous re-extract added here is guarded on rendering_device plus the validity of pipeline and blob_buffer rather than trusting them, because init_compute()'s return value is not visible from the caller and TerrainGeneratorSculpt.run_compute writes to blob_buffer without checking it. THIRD: collision. create_mesh calls _create_collision, which skips trimesh generation above 30k triangles; dab's surface area is about three times stack's, so a dab placement may come out without collision. REACH MEASURED BY READING THE MAPS, not estimated: 23 placements in 11 map files by four paths - a bare cell in ISO_AnimatedNoise and two more in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces, a curation_station roster in Corridor_ISO_AnimatedNoise and another in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_2, sixteen exhibit_furniture#kind:plinth#size:m#mount:animated_noise_explorer across eight Trial_* museums, and two corridor pairs (voxel_noise_demo-> and mc_terrain_demo->) in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces. Not one of them names an axis key; a bare token builds an empty config dict, and GridInteractablesComponent skips _apply_artifact_config entirely when the dict is empty.
dna.was: A 1 m cube of noise that travels: _process pushed current_offset along animation_path and rebuilt the mesh every 0.15 s, forever, and the whole artifact was that motion. Two things were hidden inside it. The resolution of the sampling was a bare local literal, var resolution = 16, invisible to every map and every inspector although it decides everything about the picture. And the extractor is a STUB - create_marching_cubes_mesh tests whether a cell's eight corners straddle iso_level and then emits all six faces of a full solid cube, with no lookup table, no edge interpolation and no case index - so what has always been on screen is not the surface but the set of cells in which the field changes its mind. apply_grid_config was the single word pass, a config channel wired to nothing.
dna.note: extraction is NEW, and the word is the sequence's own verb - define a field, EXTRACT a surface. It exists because this artifact is the one place in the sequence where the question is not rhetorical: its extractor stopped one step short of the surface and left the intermediate on screen, so the four rungs can walk the whole distance in four pictures, every one of them built from the density_field the loop already computes. the ladder is the DIMENSION OF THE ANSWER - a sample, a point on an edge, a face, a cell. cells = a solid cube per straddling cell, SHIPPED, the crude honest default: a mass where a boundary was promised, 917 cells and 5502 quads. faces = the cell faces the contour actually passes through, kept only where the face's own four lattice corners disagree - a perforated stepped sheet running through the block set, 1940 distinct quads, one lattice dimension closer to the surface. corners = a marker at every lattice point above iso_level, no surface at all, the sampled field itself before any decision, 2272 of 4913 points. crossings = a marker at the linearly interpolated point on every lattice edge whose ends disagree, t = (iso - a) / (b - a), which is the exact set of vertices marching cubes would have produced and this extractor never built, 1024 of them. The ladder is the sequence's truth line in reverse: here is the field, here are the points where it crosses, here are the faces it crosses, here is the mass we settled for. MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, AND THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE DESIGN. noise_3d, the straddle test and all four extractors were re-implemented in Python against the shipped .tscn values and rasterised with a z-buffer from the sweep's own standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) at 300x300. Against cells: faces differs in 26.31 percent of the frame, corners in 35.27, crossings in 34.20; corners against crossings, 17.29. Subject share of frame 34.50 / 33.08 / 13.90 / 6.32 percent, so the point clouds really are a dust. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT KILLED: the approved rung for faces was the outer SKIN of the straddling set - a face kept only where its six-neighbour does not also straddle. It rasterises 0.00 percent different from cells. Not small, ZERO: all 3486 faces the skin discards are interior and occluded, so under an opaque material a mass and its own skin are the same photograph, and that rung would have published two identical tiles and been filed INERT for a fact about occlusion. The crossed-face reading is the nearest thing that bites, and it argues something the skin did not - not how much of the mass is drawn, but which lattice element the boundary is recorded on. trace (fourier_transform: samples|stems|ribbon; spring_demo: off|phase|wave) is the nearest relative and was refused because its rungs are a one-dimensional signal plot's vocabulary, which a volume cannot answer. workings (csg_difference_demo: outcome|trace|operands|expression) was refused for a sharper reason: workings asks how much of an operation a demonstration will DISCLOSE, and cells is not a fuller disclosure than crossings - it is a cruder extractor. Different claim, different word. resolution is SHARED, taken from riemann_pump (resolution is HOW FINE THE PARTITION IS, and the partition is that artifact's own subject) and given the same three rung names as queer_marching_cave in this same sequence, deliberately, so the two can be read against each other: there a cell size in metres, here a cell count per axis, both naming the shipped state mid. If a shared vocabulary is honest the two behave alike under it, and that is itself a check on the bench. Measured on the shipped field: coarse = 8 gives 232 straddling cells of 0.125 m, mid = 16 gives 917 of 0.0625 m, fine = 24 gives 2070 of 0.0417 m and about 24800 triangles. Capped at 24 on purpose - 32 is 3678 cells and the rebuild is a triple GDScript loop that also runs every regenerate_interval while animating, so a higher rung buys nothing and risks the watchdog. The argument is that the field is continuous and everything you see is an artefact of a sampling rate nobody was told about: same noise function, same threshold, three different objects. Neither axis re-argues fusion or metaball_count, which raymarched_metaballs, metaballs and implicit_surface_modeling already hold for how much the field merges and how many sources it has.
dna.declined: THE ENTIRE TRAVEL APPARATUS, refused by name and all four for the same reason: animation_speed, regenerate_interval, animation_path and auto_start. This artifact's premise is motion - its own Info label reads Traveling Through 4D Noise - and a rate, an interval and a direction are precisely what one PNG cannot photograph. A sweep over animation_speed would publish frames differing only in where the clock happened to be, which is the info_board fault (six identical tiles from five duration exports) with a moving subject instead of a still one. The standing arrangement offered instead is the promoted pair: the two things that are true of the field whether or not anyone is travelling through it - how finely it is sampled, and what a sample is turned into. The travel was only ever a way of showing that the field extends past the box, and extraction=corners shows the same thing in one frame by drawing the field itself. Also declined: show_wireframe, which is a material flag and not a form, and mesh_color.
dna.fixture_why: There is no RNG here of any kind - noise_3d is three hardcoded trigonometric terms and the file contains no randf, no randi and no FastNoiseLite - so the thing that has to be pinned is THE CLOCK. _process accumulates current_offset every frame and regenerates the mesh every regenerate_interval, which means two tiles captured 1.5 s apart photograph two different fields of the same artifact and the sweep would report the shutter as an axis. auto_start false freezes current_offset at Vector3.ZERO, the t=0 field and the only offset every viewer is guaranteed to have seen. Written as a bare JSON boolean, not the string false, because the sweep assigns fixture values straight onto a typed export before _ready. That pin is only safe because of the lifecycle repair recorded under rebuild_guard: until this pass, auto_start false meant NO MESH AT ALL and the fixture would have scored a blank frame INERT. frame_anchor true adds an invisible layers = 0 box the size of the sampled volume so the camera frames the FIELD rather than the extent of whatever the value being tested happened to build - corners and crossings are point clouds whose reach differs from the cube mass by up to a cell, and resolution moves the outermost block by half a cell. No dna.framing key: the subject is a 1 m cube at the origin and the three Label3D nodes do not count toward a MeshInstance3D-only AABB, so the default 1.0 should be honest - but that is an estimate, not a measurement, and it should be checked against the first sweep.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was the single word pass. It now writes each key as config_<key> metadata, re-reads the two axes against their allow-lists (an unrecognised value is dropped, not applied - the science_screen failure was a typo nothing refused), and rebuilds ONLY when a signature of every value the build reads has actually moved; a config dict naming none of these axes cannot move it. Deliberately narrow: it still ignores chunk_scale, noise_scale, iso_level and the animation knobs, because widening the channel to honour keys nobody has ever sent would be a behaviour change hiding inside a promotion. TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS. First, the lifecycle: generate_chunk was reachable only through start_animation, which _ready called only when auto_start was true, so freezing the clock produced no geometry at all. _ready now builds unconditionally and auto_start governs only whether _process advances the offset - for auto_start true, which is the .tscn's value and every placement's, the end state is identical (one chunk at offset zero, is_animating true). Second, the scriptless root: the .tscn root carries no script, the script sits on the child MeshInstance3D NoiseChunk, and the promotion brief expected that to make the axis unreachable from all 11 maps. READ THE ENGINE, IT DOES NOT. GridInteractablesComponent._apply_artifact_config falls through to _config_holder, a breadth-first search for the first descendant that handles config, which finds NoiseChunk; it sets the metadata there and calls apply_grid_config on it, and all of that happens BEFORE parent_node.add_child, so the child's _ready sees the keys. capture_config_sweep._holder_of does the same for the bench. So no forwarder script was added to the root: the gap the brief describes was closed at the call site, and adding a second handler would only have given the axis two homes. The only node this script creates is the frame anchor and it is tracked in an _owned array - GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to spawned artifacts, so freeing every child is never safe here.

(4) ONE curation_station roster, Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_0, which DOES call apply_grid_config - with exactly {"emissive": false}, a key no build path reads - so the new guarded body stamps config_emissive into metadata, recomputes the signature, finds it unchanged and returns before any teardown. dna.was: a 3 x 5 grid of fifteen frozen marching-cubes cells, and a bare `pass` where apply_grid_config should be - line 431, no assignment behind it, so the artifact was unreachable from a map token by any key whatsoever. The two knobs it did expose were show_wireframes and show_labels, both true, both reachable only through a keyboard shortcut in a demo whose UI Control ships visible = false; and show_wireframes did not even do what the W key printed, because the wireframe nodes were never tracked, so toggling it changed nothing at all until a regenerate. dna.note: workings is SHARED, taken from csg_difference_demo (boolean_surfaces.json), whose note says 'workings is the axis a demonstration wants and an artwork does not: how much of the operation it is willing to show.' 26 tokens carried the word before this promotion. It transplants here because this is the same kind of object asked the same question - a demonstration, not a work - and because all four of its rungs are answerable in full, which is the test implicit_surface_modeling applied when it REFUSED sierpinski_pyramid's `packing`. What the four mean for a lookup table: expression is SHIPPED - the sheets, the fifteen wireframe cages, the 120 red/blue corner beads and the fifteen billboard labels each ending 'Config: %d', which is the table entry itself; outcome is the fifteen sheets ALONE, finished geometry with no account of where it came from and no configuration number; operands is cage and beads with NO sheet - the field before the decision, which is exactly and only what marching cubes consumes, and an inverse silhouette of outcome; trace is expression plus a marker on every one of the twelve cage edges whose two ends disagree, standing at the interpolated crossing, computed with the generator's own formula so the mark is WHERE the extracted vertex is rather than near it. WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE SIBLING, said plainly: over there the operands are two solids and `trace` is the removed material put back as a ghost, so its ladder is about a volume; here the operand is eight numbers and trace is a set of POINTS, so the ladder is about a sampling. Same question, two ontologies of showing. margin is a NEW word, and it is the sequence's truth line - 'define a field, extract a surface' - turned into a knob. The demo hardcodes 0.3 for outside and 0.7 for inside against MarchingCubesGenerator's threshold of 0.5. That pair is SYMMETRIC about the threshold, so every interpolated vertex lands on the exact edge midpoint: the diagram-book picture, and an accident of two literals rather than a property of the algorithm. Slide the pair while keeping its span at 0.4 and the fifteen cases stay the same fifteen cases - same config bytes, same table entries, same topology, the same eight beads in the same eight colours in the same eight places - while every sheet slides across its cell. The table decides what the surface IS; the numbers decide where it SITS; and only one of those is in the lookup table. Values are (outside, inside) pairs and t is measured from the inside corner: even (0.30, 0.70) t=0.50 SHIPPED; starved (0.14, 0.54) t=0.10, the inside corners barely made it and the sheets hug them until the solid is slivers; swollen (0.44, 0.84) t=0.85, the sheets stand off toward the outside corners and the solid nearly fills its cell; brimming (0.48, 0.88) t=0.95, the limit case. BOTH numbers of every pair stay strictly off 0.50 on purpose: march_cube_fixed's sign test is `density < threshold`, so an outside value of exactly 0.50 flips into the inside class, the configuration collapses to 0 or 255 and the cell renders NOTHING. Two implementation details are load-bearing rather than tidy. The chunk FILL moves with the pair (create_voxel_chunk_from_case takes _outside_value(), not a literal): the chunk is 2x2x2, so seven neighbour cubes share corners with the case cube and draw their own sheets wherever a case corner is inside, and leaving the fill at 0.3 would put those seven at a different crossing from the one the rung is arguing - the cell would contradict itself. And the bead colours are computed from the SAME resolved array the chunk got, so they are identical at all four rungs by construction rather than by luck. Words considered and rejected for this axis, each because it already carries a different claim elsewhere: `bias` (pixel_cloud), `crossing` (sine_space, sine_space_explanation, fluency_seam), and `reading`. margin names the quantity actually being varied - the distance of each sample from the threshold. NOT RE-ARGUED: fusion and metaball_count are held by raymarched_metaballs/metaballs/implicit_surface_modeling (one scene, three names) and both bite hard, so 'how much the field merges' and 'how many sources' are taken; neither is asked here.
dna.declined: REFUSED BY NAME: `animate_threshold` (line 106 as shipped, the A key, and the only thing _process has ever done). It is a time-domain export twice over - it oscillates on sin(animation_time), and what it writes is material.emission_energy, a brightness ramp - so a still photographs one arbitrary phase and a sweep over it would measure the shutter rather than the artifact. Worse, its NAME promises this sequence's central question and delivers a glow: it does not move a threshold at all, it modulates emission on meshes that were already built. margin is the honest version of what that export pretends to be, and the export is left exactly as it shipped (false, untouched, still on the A key). Also refused: case_spacing and case_scale - layout magnitudes that an AABB-fitted capture camera cancels almost exactly, since scaling every cell and the gaps between them scales the subject and the frame together; and zoom_speed / min_zoom / max_zoom, which drive the scene's own Camera3D, a node _suppress_embedded_chrome hides at spawn and no capture ever looks through.
dna.fixture_why: ONE entry, and it is a BENCH SWITCH rather than a pin - the word, the two values and the gate are csg_union_demo's and csg_intersection_demo's, character for character. Nothing here needs pinning: there is no rotation, no RNG and no animation on any default path. What does need fixing is the FRAME. Both axes change the very MeshInstance3D set that capture_config_sweep._subtree_aabb measures - workings=outcome deletes fifteen PRIMITIVE_LINES cages and 120 corner beads, and margin slides every interpolated vertex, so the subject's own box runs from 8.79 m wide at starved to 9.02 m at brimming - and a camera fitted per variant photographs each rung at its own magnification, which is the frame-relative verdict already recorded from the PostCrisis pass. capture_anchor=on stands an invisible layers=0 BoxMesh over the union of every value's extent, sized by construction from GRID_COLS/GRID_ROWS/case_spacing/case_scale and the margin table rather than measured from the built scene, so the box is identical at all sixteen combinations. Derived, its local corners are (-4.04, -0.04, -2.04) to (4.975, 0.975, 2.975): 9.015 x 1.015 x 5.015, diagonal 10.366. This is a CORRECTION to the approved design, which estimated the anchor at about 8.0 x 2.5 x 4.5 - the true box is wider and much flatter, because the sheets in the seven neighbour cubes of each 2x2x2 chunk reach 1 + t past the case corner while nothing reaches above 1 + t in y either. The gating is load-bearing rather than tidy: this box is also what capture_multi_angle frames and what sync_footprints reads, and 9.015 m where the registry records 8.79 would re-rate the artifact's footprint on the next measurement sweep. It defaults to 'off' and _read_metadata_overrides deliberately does not read config_capture_anchor, so no map token can switch it on; only direct property assignment - which is what dna.fixture and the sweep do - reaches it. Grounding is unaffected in either case: _auto_ground_artifact reads only min_y, and the anchor's -0.04 is the corner beads' own minimum, the number the artifact has always grounded on.
dna.framing_why: DERIVED ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT - I have not run Godot, and the first sweep should correct this. The rig places the camera at radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so the frame's world half-extent is simply radius * 1.9 * framing. The capture anchor's diagonal is 10.366, radius 5.183, giving a 19.7 m square frame at framing 1.0. The subject is a WIDE FLAT SLAB - 9.015 x 1.015 x 5.015 - and the canonical standpoint is yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, so its projected bounding box is about 10.25 m across (4.5075*cos(35.5) + 2.5075*sin(35.5), doubled) by about 3.37 m tall: roughly 8.9 percent of frame as a BOUNDING box, and the fifteen cells are a sparse grid inside that box, so measured subject share would land nearer 3-4 percent - under the ~6 percent floor at which a fit-by-diagonal shot of a flat subject stops being able to tell a real axis from a dead one. 0.8 gives a 15.8 m frame, roughly 14 percent bounding, and leaves the widest rung at 65 percent of frame width, nowhere near cropped (the crop limit is framing 0.52). The approved design specified 1.0 with 0.8 named as the contingency if a first sweep came in under 6 percent; the arithmetic above is why the contingency is taken up front instead. The labels sit 1.5 below the grid and 2.5 below the frame centre, well inside a 6.3 m half-height, so expression and trace do not lose their Config lines to the crop.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`. It now stamps config into metadata, re-reads it, and returns early on an unchanged signature (workings, margin, case_spacing, case_scale) - and returns immediately if _ready has not built yet. Eleven of the twelve placements never call it and the twelfth passes one key nothing reads, so not one of them is even torn down. The build is synchronous in _ready with no call_deferred anywhere on the build path. Teardown is restricted to an _owned array: the OLD KEY_R handler and the old _exit_tree both walked get_children() and freed everything, which is the CameraController this script caches, the Lighting rig, the WorldEnvironment, the UI Control - and any _RotationTimer GridInteractablesComponent attaches to the root after spawn. _rebuild() also remove_child()s before queue_free()ing, so the old nodes leave the AABB in the same frame rather than at the end of it, which is what a capture measuring straight after a config change would otherwise photograph.
dna.still_note: NOTHING IN THIS ARTIFACT MOVES on any default path - fifteen static ArrayMeshes, fifteen line cages, 120 beads and fifteen billboard labels, all resolved during _ready - which is why an axis was findable here at all in a sequence where four of six artifacts run _process. The strong rung pair is workings=outcome against operands: one removes the sheets and keeps the cage, the other the reverse, so they are inverse silhouettes of the same 8 m subject and cannot both be faint. margin is a change in sheet AREA of roughly an order of magnitude on case 1 (t=0.10 to t=0.95 on a corner triangle is t squared, 0.01 against 0.90) repeated across thirteen of the fifteen cells, with the cage and the beads deliberately held still so the still reads as an argument rather than as a resize. THE WEAK RUNG, written down here rather than discovered in the verdict, is trace against expression: they differ only by up to twelve markers per cell, and the markers sit exactly on the sheet boundary where the sheet can swallow them. CROSSING_RADIUS is therefore 0.1 - deliberately LARGER than the 0.08 corner bead - and the marker material is unshaded with emission at 1.4. If the sweep still reports trace faint, the honest remedy is to make the markers louder or to draw the residual edge segment as well, not to re-word the axis. Two cells are legitimately empty of sheet at every rung and this is truthful rather than broken: case 0 is all-outside and case 14 all-inside, so march_cube_fixed skips them and the demo stands its grey no-surface indicator there instead.

dna.default: bulge=pillowed AND resolution=mid, both exact no-ops, and both SHORT-CIRCUITS rather than lookups: _bulge_amount() returns the `bulginess` export untouched at `pillowed`, _resolved_cell_size() returns `cell_size` untouched at `mid`. Neither 1.5 nor 0.5 is re-derived from a table that happens to land on the same number, so the density field, the marching loop, the edge interpolation and the vertex colours are computed from identical floats. REACH MEASURED, and the count is 3, not the 4 the design carried: a bare grid cell in ISO_Caves (interactables[6][6]), a bare cell in Corridor_ISO_Caves (interactables[16][2]), and a `curation_station#artifacts:mc_torus_sculpture,mc:sphere,fifteen_cases_demo,queer_marching_cave,mc_shapes_gallery` roster in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_0. ISO_Showcase_12 was counted as a fourth because its map_info.description reads "Test: metaball_world + queer_marching_cave" - its interactables layer holds rhizome_cave_demo, marching_cubes and marchingcave and NOT this token. The description is stale; counting it would have been counting a sentence. None of the three passes a config key, so apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` until this pass - reaches no assignment and the guarded rebuild below is unreachable from every map that exists.
dna.was: Eight exports and an apply_grid_config whose entire body was the word `pass`. The artifact's own declared critical_parameter, bulginess, was welded at 1.5, so its truth line - "the difference between geology and architecture is just parameter choice" - was argued at exactly one parameter choice, which is the fault `fusion` was promoted to fix on the metaballs next door. The cell size was an export named `resolution` that no scene, no map and no caller has ever set. And the four noise fields were seeded from four bare randi() calls, so "the same cave twice" was not something this artifact could do.
dna.note: bulge is GEOLOGY OR ARCHITECTURE, and it is the artifact's own word - the code already calls the generator bulge_noise and the parameter bulginess, which is the `fusion` pattern: the artifact's own truth made variable, in the artifact's own vocabulary. bulginess does two things in calculate_density_at_position: it warps the sample point by up to bulginess * 10 m of cellular noise, and it scales the primary noise read at the warped point, which then enters the density sum at 0.5 weight. pillowed = 1.5 SHIPPED. gridded = 0.0 is the artifact's own stated null - the term is multiplied by bulginess twice over, so at zero the warp vanishes exactly and what is left is simplex noise plus a vertical gradient plus a smoothstep boundary, the "gridded-out rock" the desire line says it is trying not to be. rounded = 0.75 is the half-step where the warp is legible AS a warp. engulfed = 2.5, deliberately not 3.0: at 0.5 weight the bulge term already swings about +/-1.25 against other terms of similar magnitude, and a higher value risks a wholly solid or wholly empty field - the empty one photographs as NO RENDER, which the critic reads as a dead axis rather than an overdriven one. resolution is HOW FINELY THE FIELD IS SAMPLED, the second half of the sequence's own gap, and it argues against this artifact's own emerges line, "the cubes-and-cases substrate vanishes into the sensed roundness of the result". At coarse it does not vanish. mid = 0.5 m SHIPPED (21x13x21 samples, 20x12x20 marched cells); coarse = 1.0 m (11x7x11 samples, 600 cells - half-metre plates you can read the lattice off); fine = 0.3 m (34x21x34 samples, ~21,800 cells). Three rungs and not four: 0.2 m is ~75,000 samples and ~525,000 FastNoiseLite calls inside _ready, a watchdog risk that buys no extra argument. Same field, same threshold, same noise - only the sampling moves, and the claim of roundness turns out to be a claim about a cell size. The WORD is shared, taken from riemann_pump ("resolution is HOW FINE THE PARTITION IS ... the partition is this artifact's own subject", rungs pump|coarse|mid|fine) and from sphere_mid (coarse|mid|fine|ultra), and declared here with the shipped state named `mid` so the three can be read against each other. When a shared vocabulary is honest the siblings measure ALIKE, which is itself the check.
dna.rename: THE ONE PLACE THE DESIGN COULD NOT BE FOLLOWED LITERALLY. The cell size shipped as `@export var resolution: float = 0.5`, so the shared word was already spent on the number, and an axis name has to be a settable property. riemann_pump and sphere_mid both keep the named rung on `resolution` and the magnitude on a second property (n_strips; rings and radial_segments), so matching them means the float moves to `cell_size` and `resolution` becomes the enum. VERIFIED BY READING that nothing sets the old property: QueerMarchingCave.tscn does not, noise_terrain_with_blobs_demo.tscn instances the scene with a bare `[node ... instance=ExtResource]` line and overrides nothing, no map passes any key to this token, and set_cave_parameters never handled it. get_cave_info() still reports the NUMBER under the key "resolution" - at the shipped defaults the same 0.5 - so its one external contract is unchanged, with the rung added alongside as "resolution_rung". _read_metadata_overrides also accepts a NUMERIC config_resolution and routes it to cell_size, so a token written against the old name lands somewhere instead of being dropped as an unknown rung.
dna.declined: REFUSED BY NAME as time-domain: color_shift_speed and pulse_intensity. They are the only thing _process does - animate_cave_colors writes emission_energy = 1.8 + sin(time * speed) * intensity and lerps the albedo on a second sinusoid - so they are a rate and an animation phase, and a still photographs one arbitrary moment of them. Two frames of the SAME value taken 1.5 s apart would differ, which is the metaballs clock trap. They are pinned by the fixture instead of promoted. Also refused: vertical_bias and cave_density, which are real and visible but are magnitudes on the same density sum that `bulge` already varies, so they would say one thing twice; and cave_size, which is extent, and extent self-cancels under a camera that fits the subject. primary_noise_scale / secondary_noise_scale were considered for the second axis and dropped in favour of resolution: they change the FIELD, whereas resolution changes what the extractor is allowed to see of it, which is the sequence's question.
dna.fixture_why: THE DESIGN BRIEF SAID THIS ARTIFACT WAS SEEDED. IT WAS NOT, AND THAT IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING FINDING OF THE PASS. setup_noise_generators() called randi() four times, once per FastNoiseLite, from Godot's globally-seeded RNG, and regenerate_cave() did it four more. Every instantiation was a different cave, so an unfixed sweep would have photographed twelve unrelated objects and reported the difference between them as an axis - a confident bite number about nothing. cave_seed was added as a new int export where 0 means "keep the shipped randi() calls exactly, in the same order, consuming the global stream identically" (the metaball_seed pattern, and the only way to preserve behaviour that is itself random), and any other value derives the four seeds as seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3, assigned BEFORE the first get_noise_3d call. 20260811 pins them. The two zeros freeze animate_cave_colors so emission_energy is a constant 1.8 and the albedo lerp is a constant, which makes two frames of the same variant byte-comparable. Both are written as NUMBERS, never as the strings "0.0": a typed float export rejects a string assigned before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config stamps every incoming key as config_* metadata, re-reads the overrides, then compares an eleven-field signature (both rungs, cave_seed, the two RESOLVED floats, cave_size, iso_level, cave_density, vertical_bias and the two noise scales) against the one taken before the stamp. Unchanged means return, because a rebuild here is a whole density field plus a whole marching pass plus a new ConcavePolygonShape3D. It also returns early when _built is false, which is the normal case - config lands before _ready, the values are stashed as metadata, and _ready reads them, so the artifact is built once and not twice. NOTHING IS FREED and no _owned array is needed: this script creates no child nodes at all, it writes into the scene's own $CaveMesh.mesh and $CaveCollision/CollisionShape.shape, so the _RotationTimer GridInteractablesComponent attaches to this root after spawn is never in reach. The rebuild also does NOT call setup_noise_generators(): at cave_seed 0 that would draw four fresh randi() values and silently re-roll the cave underneath a config key that only moved `bulge`. The seeds are re-applied only when the cave is pinned.
dna.kin: noise_terrain_with_blobs (randomness.json, 1 placement, TestMap_Unused_10) is NOT a second registry name on this scene - it is a WRAPPER that instances QueerMarchingCave.tscn as a child alongside a Camera3D, a fog Environment, a particle field and a 100 m atmospheric sphere. It is named here because it is the one other place this density function runs, and because its instance line overrides no property at all: it inherits every default including cave_seed=0, so it is untouched by this pass and would have been moved by anything that changed the defaults. It should not be declared on these axes - a sweep of it would photograph the sphere.
